### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-core`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **23** documentable anchor(s).

**20** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e3bdc748841f8ec72aedc3d795227273f25c6baa`.

⛔ **7** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **182** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e3bdc748841f8ec72aedc3d795227273f25c6baa` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `beadeb4385340fea119683f846c3890a4aa19151` — the merge of head `3865f313b1a255282a29c8831f82d6a2ec97bc66` into base `e3bdc748841f8ec72aedc3d795227273f25c6baa`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin beadeb4385340fea119683f846c3890a4aa19151 && git checkout beadeb4385340fea119683f846c3890a4aa19151
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e3bdc748841f8ec72aedc3d795227273f25c6baa 3865f313b1a255282a29c8831f82d6a2ec97bc66 && git checkout -B drift-repro e3bdc748841f8ec72aedc3d795227273f25c6baa && git merge --no-ff 3865f313b1a255282a29c8831f82d6a2ec97bc66

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e3bdc748841f8ec72aedc3d795227273f25c6baa
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs e3bdc748841f8ec72aedc3d795227273f25c6baa` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Head-sha: `b85886609d6c2c02ee7ed5e0c1d9740c5b728cd3`

Scope: packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/19.knowledge-source-save-refused-without-knowledge-service.ts + packages/metadata-core/src/knowledge-source-save-admission.ts, packages/runtime/src/knowledge-service-lookup.ts, packages/runtime/src/domain-handler-registry.ts, packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/meta.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp-authoring.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts

The remainder of the diff (three test files, the two changesets as prose) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`; the changeset lines are read here only for section ② and for point 2.

### ① Derived judgments

- Authorable accept-set: nothing moves. No schema key, accepted value or metadata type is added or refused; entry 19 keeps its id and changes prose in `surface` and `acceptanceCriteria` only. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right.
- Refusal set at the save doors: unchanged. A scope-relative miss was already refused `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` (it folded into `undefined` and took the no-service sentence); it is still `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`, with a different sentence. No save that was refused is now accepted, and none that was accepted is now refused. Right.
- Save-door bytes: the `save` row of `DOOR_WORDING` reproduces the pre-change sentences of `noKnowledgeServiceRefusal` and `unavailable` byte for byte (read against the removed lines). Right.
- Duplicate-door answer: status and code unchanged; the message text changes (`cannot be copied`, `duplicate the package again`, no second "nothing was written"). Message text is not a published accept-set. Right.
- Public surface of `@objectstack/metadata-core`: it GROWS. `packages/metadata-core/src/index.ts:104` is `export * from './knowledge-source-save-admission.js'`, so the entry gains the names `knowledgeServiceNotInScope`, `KnowledgeServiceNotInScope` and `KnowledgeSourceSaveDoor`, and `authoredKnowledgeSourceRefusal` gains the optional input `door`. The PR declares this as no surface change. Wrong: see S1.
- Public surface of `@objectstack/runtime`: it GROWS. `DomainHandlerDeps` is re-exported at `packages/runtime/src/index.ts:281`; it gains the optional member `classifyServiceOrLoud`, and `ClassifiedServiceLookup` becomes reachable through that member's return type (it was a module-local alias in `http-dispatcher.ts`, under a comment that said "Nothing published gains a member"). The PR body's "adds nothing to the package index" is true of the re-export list and is not the test: `references/execution-duties.md` defines the public surface as what the built entry declaration reaches, re-exported names plus every type reachable through their props, parameters and return types, and says not to count the re-export list alone. Wrong as declared: see S1.
- Point 1, plumbing or fork: additive runtime plumbing, not a contract fork. The member is optional; a deps without it is read through `resolveServiceOrLoud` and answers both misses as before (`knowledge-service-lookup.ts`, the `typeof ... !== 'function'` arm); no existing member changes meaning; `resolveServiceOrLoud` still returns the service or `undefined`; the dispatcher's `classifyService` body is untouched. It follows the `isRequestKernelReady` precedent in the same interface (optional, fail-safe fallback stated in the jsdoc). Nothing here needs the decision box. It is still a widening of an exported type, which is what S1 is about.

### ② Semver level

- Level: `patch` on `@objectstack/metadata-core`, `@objectstack/runtime` and `@objectstack/spec` is right. AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3: the level follows the `Metadata-protocol` kind alone, `none` takes `patch`, and a non-protocol widening ships `patch`. All three packages are moved by the diff and all three are listed.
- `Metadata-protocol: none`: right.
- `Clause-②: no`: wrong. The line should read `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, naming what grew.

S1 (should-fix) — the `Clause-②:` declaration is `no` on the claim comment 7234905717, the PR body and `.changeset/38058-knowledge-save-refusal-scope-miss-and-duplicate-wording.md`, and the diff enlarges the public surface of two packages (section ①: three new entry names and an optional input on `@objectstack/metadata-core`; an optional member and a newly reachable type on `@objectstack/runtime`'s exported `DomainHandlerDeps`). By `references/execution-duties.md` (the criterion is "widens the accept-set or enlarges the public surface", the surface is what the built entry declaration reaches) and `references/domains/spec.md` ("however small") that is `yes`. Pending notes on `main` declare the same shapes that way at `patch`: `.changeset/37864-capability-unavailable-languages.md` (`@objectstack/runtime` `HttpDispatcherResult.response` gains an optional member), `.changeset/37828-localized-refusal-vary-accept-language.md` (`@objectstack/types` gains two exports), `.changeset/37516-kanban-uncategorized-past-page.md` (an entry-exported function gains an optional parameter). Fix: `Clause-②: yes (widening)` followed by the named additions, on all three carriers; the level stays `patch`. No tier was dodged by the wrong line: the spec path already put this PR at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`. The changeset and PR-body edits are prose-face; the claim comment is the carrier the queue gate reads.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev flag, "`DomainHandlerDeps` gained an optional member: treated as additive runtime plumbing ..., flag if the seat reads it as needs_decision": answered in ①. Additive, no fork, no decision needed; the declaration line is S1.
- Dev flag, runs outside the verify lock (one cli test re-run, one route-envelope re-run) and `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` not measured locally: the head's check-runs answer these families; see the CI reading below.
- `open_questions`: empty. Nothing to answer.
- Point 4, the two out-of-scope notes in the PR's Acceptance notes. Both should be follow-up cards; neither is filed.
  - Note 1 (the knowledge service's own verdict text through the duplicate door): yes, file it. `packages/services/service-knowledge/src/knowledge-service.ts` composes `was not saved` (3149), `Nothing was written; try again.` (3157) and `have someone who may query it save the source` (3215, 3226, 3228), and `refuseDuplicatedKnowledgeSources` appends a service verdict verbatim. These are the answers a duplicate gets on a deployment that DOES run the platform's service, which is the common path, so card #38058's fourth Acceptance line ("tells the caller to duplicate again, and says nothing was copied once") holds for the three predicate-composed sentences and not for the service's own. Same defect class as N5, same grade (p3, wording). The fix needs the door to reach `admitAuthoredSource`, so it is its own card on `@objectstack/service-knowledge`.
  - Note 2 (the REST transport): yes, file it. `RestServer.resolveKnowledgeService` (`packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts:6227`) returns whatever `kernelServiceProvider` answers and maps only the branded miss to `undefined`, so a scoped factory that answers nothing for the environment most likely still reads as "this deployment runs no knowledge service" on REST `PUT /meta/knowledge_source/:name`, the first door entry 19 names. After this PR the two transports of the same save can answer the same miss with different sentences. Unmeasured, as the PR says; the card should measure it first, then give REST the same classification or state why not. p3.
- SQL push-down (Prime Directive 5): the diff adds no data read, no id materialisation and no in-app join. The duplicate door's per-item lookup is a service-registry read, as before. No finding.
- Author: PR `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no off-relay write to name.
- Security: the scope sentence echoes the request's own resolved environment id to a caller already past `manage_metadata` and `manage_knowledge_sources`. No new disclosure.

### ④ Design judgment

**`19.knowledge-source-save-refused-without-knowledge-service.ts` (hits).** Holds. `surface` now reads "a deployment whose stack neither declares `requires: ['knowledge']` nor ships a `knowledgeSources` entry, and whose host mounts no `KnowledgeServicePlugin`". Against the code it cites: `packages/spec/src/kernel/platform-capabilities.ts` gives the `knowledge` row `mountedBy: { collection: 'knowledgeSources' }`; `stackItemCapabilities` (`packages/core/src/capability-composition.ts`) adds the token whenever the stack holds an item of that collection, at the top level or in a package body; `packages/core/src/capability-providers.ts` mounts `KnowledgeServicePlugin` for the token. So a stack that ships a source mounts the service and its author's save is admitted, and the old text over-included it. The new `acceptanceCriteria` names both mounts. No generated artifact carries the old sentence (searched the head tree for the entry id and the old wording: the two changesets and the entry only). `replacement` and `reason` are untouched and still true of the no-service branch.

**Point 2, the DELIBERATE CORRECTION.** The note is `.changeset/37983-knowledge-source-save-needs-the-service.md`, its `## FROM → TO` line. It is PENDING on `main`: the file is in the top level of `.changeset/` on `origin/main`, not under `.changeset/pre/` (the consumed stock, 1185 files, none of them this one), its only commit is `d59478f1b1` (#38013, 2026-11-28T03:46Z), and the last version pass is `9d111a7f52` (#38032, 2026-11-28T02:16Z), before it; no `CHANGELOG.md` carries it. Before: "A deployment whose stack does not declare `requires: ['knowledge']`, where authors save knowledge sources → add `requires: ['knowledge']` to the stack, restart, then save the source." After, the corrected sentence: "A deployment whose stack neither declares `requires: ['knowledge']` nor ships a `knowledgeSources` entry, where authors save knowledge sources → add `requires: ['knowledge']` to the stack, restart, then save the source." The corrected sentence is true of the code, by the same three reads as the entry above: the refusal fires only when no `knowledge` service is registered, and a shipped `knowledgeSources` entry registers one. The correction is right to make: the base sentence told a stack that already ships a source to perform a migration it does not need, card #38058 names this line in its What and its Acceptance, and the note would otherwise ship that sentence in the `CHANGELOG.md` of four packages. One line changed; the frontmatter, both declaration lines and the ADR-0087 marker of the note are untouched. The `Check Changeset` red on this head is exactly this: its one failing step is the foreign-changeset rule naming this file, and every other step of the job is green. This record confirms the correction on this head; it stands as the confirming record once S1 and S2 are closed by the delta.

**`knowledge-source-save-admission.ts`.** Agrees with its contract. The brand is a `Symbol.for` key on a frozen object, so it survives a second copy of the module and cannot collide with a real service. Order of the arms is right: engine write first (never asked, pinned), then lookup fault (`503`, could not be judged), then `undefined` or `null` (no service), then the brand (scope sentence), then the duck-typed `admitAuthoredSource`. The scope sentence says only what the lookup knows: a registration exists and served no instance for the named environment; it does not say the deployment runs none and does not name `requires`. The module jsdoc is honest that only "a door whose lookup tells that miss apart" answers this way.

**`knowledge-service-lookup.ts`.** Agrees. The mapping is total over the three outcomes; the fallback for a deps without the member reproduces the old answer; the scope passed is `context.environmentId`, as before.

**`http-dispatcher.ts`.** Agrees. `classifyService` is unchanged; the new deps member binds the request kernel exactly as `resolveServiceOrLoud` does. Read against `packages/core/src/plugin-loader.ts`: an unregistered name rejects with the branded error, so on `ObjectKernel` `no-instance-in-scope` is reached only when a registered factory answered nothing, and a plain instance (what `KnowledgeServicePlugin` registers) returns before any of it. A `SCOPED` registration asked with no scope still rejects unbranded and is answered `503` as a fault.

**`domains/meta.ts`, `domains/mcp-authoring.ts`, `domains/packages.ts`.** Agree. Each replaces the same one-line lookup with the helper; `packages.ts` passes `door: 'duplicate'` and keeps the single prefix "is refused, and nothing was copied." The `itemSaveRefusal` jsdoc now parses as sentences (N4 of the card).

**`domain-handler-registry.ts`.** The member, its jsdoc and the reworded `resolveServiceOrLoud` paragraph agree with the code. One defect:

S2 (should-fix) — `packages/runtime/src/domain-handler-registry.ts`: the new `ClassifiedServiceLookup` alias and its jsdoc were inserted between the existing jsdoc of `DomainHandlerDeps` (the block that opens "The dispatcher facilities an extracted domain body is allowed to use — the WHOLE dependency contract" and ends "do not cache the resolved kernel anywhere that outlives one request.") and the `export interface DomainHandlerDeps` line it documents. At head two jsdoc blocks sit back to back above the alias and the exported interface carries none, so the interface's contract text, including "Growing this interface is a design decision" and the rule against a facility that reads a kernel without the request, no longer attaches to it in the shipped declarations. Fix: move the alias and its jsdoc above the `DomainHandlerDeps` block (or below the interface). A code-file move, so it is read on the delta.

**Point 3, the pin.** Confirmed in the diff. `meta-save-capability-gate.test.ts` builds a real `ObjectKernel`, registers `knowledge` with `registerServiceFactory(..., ServiceLifecycle.SCOPED)` serving one environment, and asserts the `503`, the code, the sentence opening naming `'platform'`, the absence of "runs no knowledge service", and that nothing is saved; its control boots the same factory serving the request's environment (admitted, asked once, saved once) and a plain registered instance (the same). `packages-knowledge-source-gate.test.ts` does the same at the duplicate door on a real kernel with a scoped factory that answers nothing, with a plain-instance control that is asked once and copies. The metadata-core unit pins both sentences per door. The pins sit on the registry's own classification, not on a double.

Observations of the third grade (no effect on correctness or the contract), accepted as deviations unless a later head moves these files anyway:
- Entry 19 `acceptanceCriteria`: "(either mounts the service; or the host mounts KnowledgeServicePlugin)" is awkward; the meaning is recoverable.
- `unavailable()` picks its tail with a `door === 'save'` ternary while the other two sentences read `DOOR_WORDING`; the bytes are right.
- The scope sentence's "registered on this deployment" rests on the kernel rejecting an unregistered name with the branded error. `ObjectKernel` does. A kernel-shaped host whose `getServiceAsync` answers `null` for an unknown name would be read as registered. That is the classifier's existing premise, outside this diff.
- For the lane seat's ACCEPT (test face): the changeset says the MCP `save_metadata_draft` door tells the scope miss apart; no pin exercises that door for it. The wiring is the shared helper pinned at the other two doors.
